about: Email server settings, each value taken from the provider's own documentation. A null with a note in "undocumented" means the provider does not state that value, not that it is unknown.

providers.name: AOL Mail
providers.authentication: An app password from your AOL Account Security page — unless your app signs in through AOL’s own sign-in page.
notes: IMAP keeps the app and mail.aol.com in sync; POP only downloads the Inbox.

providers.name: AT&T Mail
providers.authentication: A secure mail key (16 characters, created in your AT&T profile) — unless your app signs in with OAuth, where your AT&T password works.
notes: AT&T also lists port 587 for the IMAP outgoing server.
With POP3, the outgoing server is outbound.att.net on port 465 with SSL.

providers.name: CenturyLink Email
providers.authentication: Use your regular CenturyLink email password.
notes: CenturyLink moved all email to a new service in October 2022 — apps set up before then may need these updated settings.
qwestoffice.net uses different servers (pop.qwestoffice.net and smtp.qwestoffice.net).

providers.name: Cox Email (Yahoo)
providers.authentication: A Yahoo app password — your regular password won’t work in email apps.
notes: Cox moved all cox.net email to Yahoo Mail; Yahoo now handles cox.net email support.

providers.name: EarthLink
providers.authentication: Use your full email address and password. Authentication is required.
notes: For POP, other EarthLink domains use pop. plus the domain — for example pop.mindspring.com or pop.peoplepc.com.
If you use more than one device, put them all on IMAP; EarthLink warns that mixing POP and IMAP can stop messages saving.

providers.name: Fastmail
providers.authentication: An app password — Fastmail doesn’t accept your regular password in email apps.
notes: Don’t turn on Secure Password Authentication (SPA) — it isn’t needed with SSL/TLS and won’t work.
If your network blocks these ports, Fastmail offers proxy servers (imaps-proxy, pops-proxy, smtps-proxy.fastmail.com).

providers.name: Frontier Mail
notes: Frontier’s settings page lists POP3 and SMTP only — no IMAP server.

Current email-app authentication is unconfirmed: the Yahoo web sign-in guide does not establish a mail-client method; an older Frontier guide mentions password authentication for outgoing mail without specifying its type.

providers.name: Gmail
providers.authentication: Use your app’s “Sign in with Google” option where available. If you use 2-Step Verification and your app can’t sign in with Google, Google suggests an app password.
notes: IMAP is always on for personal Gmail accounts.
POP has to be turned on first in Gmail settings under Forwarding and POP/IMAP.
Work or school accounts: check with your administrator for the correct SMTP configuration.

providers.name: GMX
providers.authentication: Use your regular GMX password, or an application-specific password in email programs when two-factor authentication is enabled.
notes: POP3 and IMAP are switched off by default. Turn them on in your GMX email settings first.
Your app must support TLS 1.2 or 1.3 — older TLS versions are no longer accepted.

providers.name: GMX (gmx.net)
providers.authentication: Use an App-Passwort for external email apps. The German help page lists the normal password as a possible cause of problems; an App-Passwort is required with two-factor authentication and for access from outside Europe, the US and Canada.
notes: POP3 or IMAP has to be switched on in your GMX settings before you can use them.
Your app must support TLS 1.2 or 1.3.

providers.name: GoDaddy Professional Email
providers.authentication: Your email password — not your GoDaddy account password.
notes: Microsoft 365 from GoDaddy uses Microsoft’s servers instead; GoDaddy recommends Exchange settings or Outlook on the web for it.
Older Workspace Email accounts use the same IMAP and SMTP servers. GoDaddy is retiring Workspace Email.

providers.name: iCloud Mail
providers.username: IMAP: usually the part of your address before the @ (try the full address if that fails). SMTP: your full iCloud address.
providers.authentication: An app-specific password, generated from your Apple Account — not your normal Apple password.
notes: iCloud Mail doesn’t support POP.
On Apple devices that meet iCloud’s requirements, use the built-in iCloud settings instead.
Thunderbird uses the documented usual IMAP local part and full SMTP address; if IMAP fails, Apple recommends trying the full address.

providers.name: Juno
providers.authentication: Use your Juno email password. For outgoing mail, select Require Sign-in.
notes: Juno publishes no IMAP server — POP3 only. Set “Delete email from server” to Never so a second device and webmail can still see your mail.
Outgoing mail needs authentication: tick Require Sign-in on the SMTP server.
Juno’s help pages have not been revised in years — its setup page still lists Outlook Express. Re-check these values against Juno before relying on them.

providers.name: mail.com
providers.authentication: Use your regular mail.com password. Application-specific password support is not confirmed by the cited troubleshooting page.
notes: POP3, IMAP and SMTP are mail.com Premium features only — free accounts use the website or the mail.com Mail app.
Access is switched off by default: Email › Settings › POP3 & IMAP › “Enable access to this account via POP3 and IMAP”. mail.com turns it off again after long non-use.
Application-specific password support needs a separate first-party source before it can be added to auth_methods.

providers.name: Microsoft 365
providers.authentication: Your work or school account password. Turn on “My outgoing server requires authentication” and leave Secure Password Authentication off.
notes: Your organisation’s administrator can turn POP, IMAP or SMTP off for your mailbox. If these settings don’t work, ask them first.
Accounts operated by 21Vianet (China) use different servers.

providers.name: NetZero
providers.username: Conflicting instructions: NetZero Member ID or full email address
providers.authentication: Use your NetZero email password. Outgoing mail requires sign-in.
notes: NetZero publishes no IMAP server — POP3 only. Set “Delete email from server” to Never so a second device and webmail can still see your mail.
Webmail is on netzero.net; addresses and mail servers are on netzero.com. A hostname that looks almost right is usually this.
Outgoing mail needs authentication: tick Require Sign-in on the SMTP server.

Username conflict: NetZero POP settings and older Outlook Express/Mac Mail guides specify Member ID without @netzero.com; its Thunderbird and separate manual Mac Mail instructions use the full email address. No automatic username mapping.

providers.name: Optimum Email
providers.authentication: The password for your email address. Turn on “My outgoing server requires authentication”.
notes: Optimum recommends IMAP if you read email on more than one device.

No first-party server settings found in the supplied source review. The cited webmail guide concerns added mail accounts, not Optimum's own incoming/outgoing servers. Retained historical values are unverified; do not generate configurations.

providers.name: Outlook.com
providers.authentication: Your Microsoft account password. Outlook.com requires an app that supports Modern Auth (OAuth2).
notes: POP and IMAP access are off by default. Turn them on in Outlook.com under Settings › Mail › Forwarding and IMAP.

providers.name: Spectrum Email (Bright House)
providers.authentication: Your Spectrum email password. Outgoing mail requires authentication.
notes: Spectrum lists IMAP with SSL on, incoming port 993 and outgoing port 587.
Spectrum's first-party guidance lists SSL on and SMTP port 587, but does not distinguish implicit TLS from STARTTLS. SMTP security remains undocumented.

providers.name: Spectrum Email (Charter)
providers.authentication: Your Spectrum email password. Outgoing mail requires authentication.
notes: Spectrum lists IMAP with SSL on, incoming port 993 and outgoing port 587.
Spectrum's first-party guidance lists SSL on and SMTP port 587, but does not distinguish implicit TLS from STARTTLS. SMTP security remains undocumented.

providers.name: Spectrum Email (Roadrunner / TWC)
providers.authentication: Your Spectrum email password. Outgoing mail requires authentication.
notes: Spectrum lists IMAP with SSL on, incoming port 993 and outgoing port 587.
Two-domain accounts (roadrunner.com / adelphia.net, mi.rr.com / twmi.rr.com, nycap.rr.com / berkshire.rr.com): sign in to email apps with the roadrunner.com, mi.rr.com or nycap.rr.com address.
Spectrum's guidance covers domains ending in .rr.com after the Bright House exceptions, not bare rr.com. SSL on with SMTP port 587 does not establish the encryption mode.

providers.name: Suddenlink Email (Optimum)
providers.authentication: The password for your email address. Turn on “My outgoing server requires authentication”.
notes: No first-party server settings found in the supplied source review. The transition page links webmail, not mail-client settings. Retained historical values are unverified; do not generate configurations.

providers.name: Verizon.net (AOL Mail)
providers.authentication: Use an app that supports OAuth2, or create an AOL app password.
notes: Verizon retired its email service; verizon.net addresses that moved to AOL use these AOL-published settings.
If your verizon.net address moved to Yahoo instead, use Yahoo Mail’s settings.

providers.name: WEB.DE
providers.authentication: Use your WEB.DE password; with two-factor authentication enabled, POP3 and IMAP programs require an application-specific password.
notes: POP3 or IMAP has to be switched on in your WEB.DE settings before you can use them.

providers.name: Windstream (Kinetic) Email
providers.authentication: Use your windstream.net email password.
notes: Windstream recommends IMAP. If one device uses IMAP, set every device to IMAP to avoid “POP lock”.
Accounts with no Webmail, POP or IMAP activity for 180 days become inactive.

providers.name: Xfinity Email (Comcast)
providers.authentication: Your Xfinity ID password. Turn on third-party access first: Xfinity Email › Settings › Security › Third Party Access Security.
notes: Port 25 isn’t supported for sending, and POP port 110 no longer works.
Xfinity recommends IMAP, so mail and folders stay in sync across devices.

providers.name: Yahoo Mail
providers.authentication: Yahoo asks you to generate an app password for third-party email apps.

providers.name: Yandex Mail
providers.username: The part of your address before the @
providers.authentication: An app password (type “Mail”) created in your Yandex ID. It’s shown only once.
notes: Turn on mail-client access first: Mail settings › Email clients › “From the imap.yandex.com server via IMAP”, plus “App passwords and OAuth tokens”.
Yandex no longer updates POP3 support and doesn’t guarantee it works.

providers.name: Zoho Mail
providers.username: Your Zoho username or full Zoho Mail address
providers.authentication: Use your Zoho account password, or an application-specific password if two-factor authentication is enabled.
notes: Turn on IMAP Access first: Settings › Mail Accounts › your address › IMAP.
Paid organisation accounts (you@yourdomain.com) use imappro.zoho.com and smtppro.zoho.com instead.
Your account’s Server Configuration Details shows the exact servers for your data centre — use those if they differ.
IMAP isn’t available to newly signed-up free-plan users.
The complete Zoho Mail address is accepted as a username; generated configurations use the full address.
